summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of stroke, atrial fibrillation, COPD, alcohol use disorder, and esophageal ulcer disease was admitted for sudden-onset epigastric abdominal pain radiating to multiple quadrants. During placement of a central venous catheter, an iatrogenic pneumothorax occurred, requiring insertion of a right pleural pigtail catheter. The patient was managed for alcohol withdrawal and acidosis, with improvement in both. Abdominal pain resolved with medical management for esophagitis and ulcer disease. The chest tube was removed after confirmation of lung re-expansion on imaging, and the patient was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for cardiac, gastrointestinal, and hematologic issues.
